IRCC Study Permit — Eligibility
sources.note: Availability-only automated check; manual review required. Confirm valid letter of acceptance from a Designated Learning Institution (DLI), PAL/TAL or Quebec CAQ requirement/exemption, sufficient funds for tuition + living expenses + return transportation, admissibility/medical or police documents if requested, and that the applicant will leave Canada when authorised stay ends. Eligibility is case-specific; an LOA or PAL/TAL does not guarantee approval. Check the applicant's nationality-specific IRCC visa-office instructions. Detection is not legal interpretation.

sources.name: Department of Home Affairs — Student visa subclass 500
sources.note: Manual counsellor review required. Verify exact CRICOS provider/course/campus and valid CoE for every intended course; CoE must remain valid at lodgement and decision. Check Genuine Student criterion and 150-word online responses, academic history, course rationale, home-country ties/economic circumstances, employment and immigration history. Run the personalised Home Affairs Document Checklist Tool using passport country and principal provider; attach financial/English evidence if listed. Published 12-month living costs: AUD 29,710 student, AUD 10,394 partner, AUD 4,449 child; add first 12 months tuition, travel, and applicable schooling costs (published guide AUD 13,502 per school-age child/year); check pro-rata method and current amounts before lodgement. Evidence must show genuine access and source of funds; one-day balance alone may be insufficient. Maintain OSHC for all applicants unless exempt. English scores/exemptions depend on current test-date rules and individual checklist. Most students may work 48 hours/fortnight while course in session; research master's/doctoral students and family may have no cap after course begins; verify VEVO/grant conditions. Since 2 Oct 2026, most applications must be lodged offshore unless applicant meets an eligible onshore category; family inclusion rules changed and need individual review. Do not guarantee work, approval, processing time or post-study outcomes. Detection is not legal interpretation.

sources.name: Immigration New Zealand — Fee Paying Student Visa
sources.note: Manual counsellor review required. Verify current approved provider and NZQA Code signatory status, exact course/campus/NZQCF level and offer of place. Tuition evidence generally required for 1 year or programme (shorter); tuition is additional to maintenance. Tertiary/English/non-compulsory study funds: NZD 20,000/year or NZD 1,667/month for shorter study; school students NZD 17,000/year or NZD 1,417/month. Also prove outward travel. Primary evidence may include 3 months of bank transactions, term deposit held 3 months, scholarship or qualifying education loan; explain deposits over NZD 2,000 and source of funds. Sri Lankan nationals may be eligible for Funds Transfer Scheme if INZ directs. Check health, character, insurance and individual checklist. Genuine intentions include course rationale, prior study, funding, immigration history and future plans. From 27 Oct 2026 eligible student work up to 25 hours/week; new master's-by-research applications on/after that date no longer have unlimited work. Relevant student visa expiry is generally 2 months after course end instead of 1 month; 31 March expiry remains unchanged. Check eVisa. PSWV depends on exact NZQCF level and study length; degree level 7+ usually 30 weeks full-time in NZ; eligible non-degree L4-7 only on INZ list and work related to study; PSWV requires at least NZD 5,000 and deadlines usually 3 months (doctoral 6 months; specific cases 12). Verify current announcements and application dates; no guaranteed job, visa or residence.

sources.name: U.S. Department of State — Student Visa (F/M categories, SEVIS and Form I-20)
sources.note: Manual counsellor review required. Verify correct F-1 or M-1 category, SEVP-certified school/programme, SEVIS registration and signed Form I-20, DS-160, academic preparation, credible funds based on the school's I-20 estimate, intent to depart after authorised study, and current Colombo post instructions. Current published fees: USD 185 nonimmigrant visa application fee (DOS) plus separate USD 350 I-901 SEVIS fee for F/M students; recheck official fee pages before payment and match the I-901 receipt to the current I-20 SEVIS ID. New F/M visas may be issued up to 365 days before course start, but new students may not enter more than 30 days before start. Visa issuance does not guarantee admission at the port of entry. Sri Lankan residents should follow current post-location guidance for their country of nationality or residence. No universal government bank-balance amount. Detection is not legal interpretation.

sources.name: GDRFA Dubai — Issuing a residency permit to a student
sources.note: Primary Dubai operational source. The educational institution is the student's host/guarantor for this non-working student residence route. GDRFA published core documents: recent colour photo with white background, passport copy, approved medical examination, Emirates ID application receipt and health insurance. Institution must be licensed and have Ministry of Education or relevant emirate education-authority approval. Published service page currently lists AED 200 residence permit fee plus AED 10 Knowledge Dirham, AED 10 Innovation Dirham, AED 500 inside-country fee (if applicable), AED 20 delivery; fees may change and are not an all-in student budget. Expected completion is listed as 48 hours, not a guarantee. Page states 60 days after expiry/cancellation. Confirm sponsor, fees, documents, timing and grace-period category directly with GDRFA/institution for each case. Detection is not legal interpretation.

sources.name: IRCC — Post-graduation work permit eligibility
sources.note: Availability-only automated check; manual case review required. General tests: eligible DLI and exact PGWP-eligible programme; programme at least 8 months (900 hours for Quebec); full-time status each semester except possible part-time final semester; apply within 180 days of completion confirmation; verify study permit/status, authorised leave, transfers, distance learning, prior PGWP and exclusions including ESL/FSL, general-interest/non-credit and public-private curriculum-licensing partnership programmes. Language: bachelor's/master's/doctoral and other university graduates CLB/NCLC 7 in all 4 skills; college/polytechnic and other non-university graduates CLB/NCLC 5 in all 4 skills. For study permit applications on/after 1 Nov 2024, non-degree university and college/non-university programmes generally also need eligible field of study; bachelor's/master's/doctoral degrees have no field restriction. Check exact 6-digit CIP 2021 code and current 2026 frozen eligible list where applicable. Duration is not automatic: usually programme length for eligible programmes under 2 years, up to 3 years for eligible programmes 2 years or longer; eligible master's of at least 8 months may qualify for up to 3 years. Passport expiry can shorten validity. Detection is not legal interpretation; never promise PGWP or a fixed duration from a course title.

sources.note: ICP student residence permit route. Educational establishment is the host/guarantor. Official listed documents include passport, personal photo, Ministry of Education or competent emirate education authority approval, university/college/institution enrolment certificate, institution/host acceptance letter specifying academic or training programme and duration, and valid health insurance; approved medical fitness, institution licence and authority approval are also required as applicable. sources.name: GDRFA Dubai — Issuing a visit visa for study, training or rehabilitation
sources.note: Separate route — NOT the ordinary student residence permit. GDRFA service is a single-entry visit visa for study/training/rehabilitation for 30, 60 or 180 days; licensed educational institution must be sponsor/host. Published core documents: one photo, passport copy with at least six months validity, and letter from educational entity stating programme and duration. Published fees vary by duration and applicant location; financial security deposit and other charges may apply. Do not describe this as student residence, do not promise conversion/extension, and confirm the applicant's intended legal stay route and conditions with GDRFA and institution before advising.

sources.name: U.S. ICE / SEVP — F-1 student employment (on-campus, CPT and OPT)
sources.note: Manual review required. F-1 on-campus work is generally limited to 20 hours/week while school is in session, subject to status and school rules. CPT must be integral to the curriculum, directly related to the major, authorised by the DSO in SEVIS and endorsed on Form I-20 before work starts; one year or more of full-time CPT removes OPT eligibility at the same education level. OPT is temporary employment directly related to the major, normally up to 12 months per education level; pre-completion use reduces the remaining allotment. Post-completion OPT requires a DSO recommendation and USCIS EAD before work. Since the 17 July 2026 final rule effective 15 September 2026, covered students generally must file post-completion OPT no later than 30 days after the I-20 programme end date (may file up to 90 days before); transitional cases depend on I-94 D/S vs fixed Admit Until Date. Qualifying STEM graduates may seek a separate 24-month extension subject to designated CIP field, employer E-Verify, Form I-983 and timely filing. Post-completion unemployment limits are generally 90 days for initial OPT and 150 days total across initial plus STEM extension. The applicable grace period may be 30 or 60 days depending on transition/I-94 status; do not give a blanket answer. Verify live USCIS/DHS and DSO guidance; never promise work or OPT.

sources.name: U.S. ICE / SEVP — I-901 SEVIS fee and payment FAQ
sources.note: Availability-only automated check; manually verify fee and payment timing immediately before advising. ICE currently lists USD 350 for F-1/M-1 students; this is separate from the nonimmigrant visa application fee. Pay only after receiving Form I-20 and use the exact SEVIS ID shown on the current I-20; check the receipt matches that ID. Required fee generally must be paid before the visa interview. Confirm exemptions, repeat-payment rules and current amount on the live ICE FAQ and official payment portal. Detection is not legal interpretation.

sources.name: USCIS — Optional Practical Training (OPT) for F-1 students
sources.note: Availability-only automated check; manual review required. OPT is temporary employment directly related to the student's major area of study, not a job placement or automatic post-study entitlement. Confirm eligibility, DSO recommendation in SEVIS, Form I-765 filing window, USCIS approval and EAD/start date before any work begins. Check unemployment limits, reporting obligations, travel/re-entry and current USCIS instructions. STEM OPT extension is a separate 24-month route with designated STEM degree/CIP code and employer/Form I-983 requirements. Never promise OPT approval or employment. Detection is not legal interpretation.

sources.name: Study in Japan — Immigration procedures, COE and financial evidence
sources.note: Availability-only automated check; manual case review required. Confirm the exact eligible school/course and Student status category; school commonly applies as proxy for the Certificate of Eligibility (COE). Check applicant/guarantor savings balance, income certificate and source-of-funds evidence against the school's current COE checklist and full study budget. COE does not guarantee visa issuance. Confirm current Japan Embassy/VFS Sri Lanka application channel, fees and checklist separately. Detection is not legal interpretation.

sources.name: Immigration Services Agency — Student permission for activities outside status (28-hour rule)
sources.note: Availability-only automated check; manual review required. Student status alone does not permit employment. Confirm advance Permission to Engage in Activity Other Than That Permitted under the Status of Residence (blanket or individual permission). General blanket permission is up to 28 hours per week; during long school holidays up to 8 hours per day. Verify the actual permission endorsement/permit and prohibited activity restrictions; do not treat work permission as automatic or guarantee a job. Detection is not legal interpretation.

sources.name: Study in Japan — Part-time work, conditions and income reality-check
sources.note: Availability-only automated check; manual review required. Official guidance says part-time work requires permission, must not interfere with study, excludes adult-entertainment businesses, and is generally limited to 28 hours weekly or 8 hours daily during long school holidays. Official page reports approximately JPY 81,000 average monthly earnings based on the 2023 survey and warns that part-time work alone cannot cover all tuition and living expenses. Treat survey data as context, not a wage promise. Detection is not legal interpretation.

sources.name: Spanish Ministry — Long-term study stay authorisation (Hoja 1)
sources.note: Availability-only automated check; manual review required. Verify eligible course category, authorised provider, admission/enrolment, minimum in-person attendance where relevant, application timing (generally at least 2 months before start), health insurance, return travel and sufficient funds. Current ministry guidance generally uses 100% of IPREM per month for student maintenance unless accommodation is prepaid for the full stay. Check the current IPREM value and filing-date rules; do not quote an outdated fixed euro amount. Detection is not legal interpretation.

sources.name: Spanish Ministry — Student work access and 30-hour weekly limit (Hoja 4 bis)
sources.note: Availability-only automated check; manual review required. For eligible higher-education study authorisations, work may be automatically permitted where compatible with studies, up to 30 hours per week, subject to applicable geographic and authorisation conditions. Do not apply this generally to all short courses or training categories. Verify current national rules and student's exact authorisation; no job or income guarantee. Detection is not legal interpretation.

sources.name: UAE Government / MoHRE — Work permits (student training and employment; part-time)
sources.note: Official UAE Government/MoHRE work-permit overview. It lists 13 permit types, including part-time work permits and a student training and employment permit. UAE Labour Law Article 6 prohibits work without a valid MoHRE permit; employer must obtain the appropriate permit. The student training/employment permit is a distinct route for a student already in the UAE, subject to conditions; it is not automatic permission attached to a student residence visa. For expatriate students, official MoHRE guidance lists valid UAE residence visa, Emirates ID/student-status evidence and (for training) an NOC from the educational institution; students aged 15–18 also require guardian consent and medical fitness. Academic-holiday recruitment may be up to three consecutive months each time under the student-specific guidance. A separate part-time permit is generally for age 18+ and must be applied for by the hiring company; eligibility and sponsor NOC requirements depend on the case. Do not promise a universal weekly-hours limit, job placement or earnings. Confirm permit type, eligibility, sponsor NOC and employer jurisdiction with MoHRE and the institution before work starts. Detection is not legal interpretation.

sources.name: UAE Government / MoHRE — Employment and training of minors (student conditions)
sources.note: MoHRE-provided official guidance: students aged 15+ may be trained/employed only under applicable permit/contract conditions. For expatriate students, required items include valid UAE residence visa, Emirates ID showing student status, medical fitness certificate, and for training an educational-institute NOC; parent/legal guardian consent applies to ages 15–18. Academic-holiday employment may be for up to three consecutive months each time. This is not proof that all university students can work freely or a stated universal term-time hours allowance. Confirm current permit type, employer application and conditions with MoHRE before work begins. Detection is not legal interpretation.

sources.name: GDRFA Dubai — Issuing a residence permit to a student
sources.note: Primary Dubai student residence service. GDRFA states that a foreign student enrolled in an accredited UAE university, college, educational institution or research institute may receive a residence permit with the institution as host and guarantor. Published checklist includes recent white-background photo, passport copy, approved medical examination, Emirates ID application receipt and health insurance; institution must be licensed and have relevant education-authority approval. The displayed service fee components are not an all-in student budget. Page also states a 60-day grace period after expiry/cancellation for this service. Confirm current fees, sponsor, documents, permit category and grace period for the individual case directly with GDRFA/institution. Availability-only automated check; detection is not legal interpretation.

sources.name: GDRFA Dubai — Renewing a student's student residence permit
sources.note: Official Dubai student residence renewal service. Lists a recent white-background photo, passport copy and approved medical examination; requires the educational institution to be licensed and to have the relevant education-authority approval. The page states a 60-day grace period after expiry/cancellation. Compare with ICP student-specific 180-day post-study guidance; confirm the student's exact permit category and grace period directly with GDRFA before advising. Availability-only check; detection is not legal interpretation.

sources.name: Visit Dubai — Earn while you learn (student work permits)
sources.authority: Dubai Department of Economy and Tourism / Visit Dubai
sources.note: Official Dubai student guidance distinguishes Student Training and Work Permit (students aged 15+ enrolled in a UAE educational institution; institution NOC for training; employer applies) from the separate Part-time Work Permit (age 18+ and only some students may qualify; sponsor/employer NOC may be required; hiring company applies). It says student work requires valid residence visa and the necessary MoHRE permit. Internship availability does not guarantee paid employment or placement. Confirm exact eligibility, employer licensing jurisdiction, permit category, NOC and conditions with MoHRE and the institution before work begins. Do not promise jobs, fixed hours or earnings. Detection is not legal interpretation.
